articles.title: Woman buys vacant Hawaiian land for $22,500 at tax auction; years later, a developer's contractor builds a $500,000 house on her property without permission, triggering a legal battle
articles.summary: A piece of land bought at a county tax auction was supposed to be a quiet investment for a California woman, something she could make use of when the time
articles.body: A piece of land bought at a county tax auction was supposed to be a quiet investment for a California woman, something she could make use of when the time was right. Instead, the property became the centre of an unexpected legal dispute after she discovered that a fully built house, valued at around $500,000, stood on the land she had purchased.Annaleine ‘Anne’ Reynolds had paid approximately $22,500 for the vacant Hawaiian plot in 2018. She was not living on the island when construction took place, and it was only in 2023 that she learnt someone had built a house on her property without her knowledge or permission. The dispute eventually went to court before being settled in 2025.How a vacant $22,500 Hawaiian plot became the site of a $500,000 homeAccording to Fortune reports, Reynolds acquired the one-acre property in Hawaiian Paradise Park, a residential subdivision in the Puna district of Hawaii's Big Island, in 2018. The purchase was made through a county tax auction, where she secured the land for about $22,500. At the time, the plot was vacant, and there was no indication that a residential development was planned for it.She was living in California during the Covid-19 pandemic and had not yet decided when she would travel to Hawaii to make use of the property. The land remained unused while she waited for a suitable opportunity to visit. That changed in 2023, when a real estate broker contacted her with information she had not expected to hear.According to a report by Hawaii News Now, the broker told Reynolds that he had sold a house built on her property. The building was worth approximately $500,000. What she had bought as an empty parcel of land had, without her involvement, become the site of a completed residential property.Who was responsible for the $500,000 house that appeared on a stranger's landThe house was part of a wider building project undertaken by Keaau Development Partnership, a local developer that had acquired several plots in Hawaiian Paradise Park. The company had engaged PJ's Construction to build roughly a dozen houses across the properties it owned in the subdivision.During that work, one of the houses was mistakenly constructed on Reynolds' land, which was not among the developer's purchased properties. The error brought several parties into conflict, including the developer, the building contractor and professionals involved in the construction process.The dispute was not simply about a misplaced building. Questions arose over who was responsible for the mistake and what should happen to a house that had been erected on privately owned land. Reynolds, the construction company, the architect and others were subsequently named in a lawsuit brought by the developer."There’s a lot of fingers being pointed between the developer and the contractor and some subs," Reynolds' lawyer, James DiPasquale, said, describing the disagreements over responsibility for the construction.The dispute over who should bear the cost of the mistakeThe developer reportedly offered Reynolds a neighbouring parcel of land of comparable size and value as a way of resolving the situation. She declined the proposal, according to court documents.Her legal position centred on the fact that she had purchased the original property and had not authorised anyone to build on it. Accepting another plot, she argued through her legal representation, would not address the underlying issue of construction taking place on someone else's land without permission.DiPasquale warned that allowing the developer or contractor to resolve the matter simply by offering an alternative property could have wider implications for landowners."It would set a dangerous precedent, if you could go on to someone else’s land, build anything you want, and then sue that individual for the value of it," he said.Reynolds also filed a counterclaim against the developer, stating that she had not known about the unauthorised building work. Her position challenged the idea that she should be held responsible for a construction decision made without her involvement.Court orders removal of wrongly built house but rejects part of Reynolds’ claimThe dispute took a significant turn in June 2024, when a Hawaii County judge ordered the removal of the house built on Reynolds' property. According to a report by KITV, the court found that the developer and construction company had assumed the risk of proceeding without a property survey. The contractor had reportedly relied on telephone poles to identify the plots rather than commissioning a survey.The judge also dismissed the developer's case against Reynolds and rejected its argument that her ownership title was invalid, finding that the developer had not provided sufficient evidence to establish that claim. However, the court did not grant her request to restore the property to its previous condition in terms of its flora and faunaDisagreement deepens over who was responsible for the mistakeThe developer's lawyer, Peter Olson, offered a different account of Reynolds' refusal to accept the neighbouring property. Speaking to The Associated Press, he said his client believed she was attempting to benefit financially from a mistake made by PJ's Construction.Olson pointed out that many of the parcels in Hawaiian Paradise Park were similar in size and layout, making the alternative property comparable to the one Reynolds had originally purchased. His comments reflected the disagreement between the parties over what would constitute a reasonable settlement.The contractor's role also came under scrutiny. An attorney representing PJ's Construction told Hawaii News Now that the developer had not wanted to hire surveyors before the building work began. The allegation raised further questions about how the construction team established property boundaries before starting the project.A years-long property dispute ends with a confidential settlementThe case highlighted the consequences of a construction project proceeding on land that did not belong to the developer. Reynolds had paid approximately $22,500 for an undeveloped acre, only to discover years later that a house worth around $500,000 had been built there without her knowledge.The legal battle continued for several years, with questions surrounding property boundaries, construction responsibility and the rights of a landowner who had not authorised the work. In May 2025, Hawaii News Now reported that the dispute between Reynolds and the developer had finally been settled, according to newly filed court documents. The terms of the settlement, however, were not made public.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. articles.title: No transactions made, no OTPs shared: Bengaluru techie loses Rs 5.5L in AMEX, RBL card fraud
articles.summary: Bengaluru techie lost Rs 5.5 lakh in unauthorised AMEX and RBL credit card transactions in an hour; case filed, experts cite data theft and breaches.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A 31-year-old software engineer lost Rs 5.5 lakh in a credit card fraud involving his AMEX and RBL Bank cards on Nov 11, after cybercriminals allegedly carried out multiple unauthorised transactions within just an hour.According to the complaint filed by Siddarth (name changed), a resident of Indiranagar, fraudulent transactions worth Rs 4,02,722 were made on his AMEX credit card, while Rs 1,44,558 was debited from his RBL Bank card. The transactions took place between 12.56 pm and 2 pm, taking the total loss to Rs 5,47,280.Siddarth told police that neither he nor his family members had shared their card details, OTPs, PINs or other confidential banking information with anyone. He also denied downloading any APK files or authorising transactions.The family became aware of the fraud after receiving notifications about the suspicious transactions. Siddarth immediately contacted both banks, got the cards blocked to prevent further losses and reported the incident to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 before approaching police.A case has been registered at the East Cyber Crime police station under the Information Technology Act and Section 318 (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Why do such frauds happen?Credit card frauds involving unauthorised transactions can occur even when victims insist they have not shared their OTPs, PINs or card details. In many cases, fraudsters exploit weaknesses in digital payment systems, steal card information through sophisticated methods or misuse compromised credentials, the officer said.However, in this case, investigation will have to establish how the card details were accessed and how the payments were authorised, he added.Another senior officer said the possibilities of siphoning off money from credit cards include card data theft: Fraudsters may obtain card numbers, expiry dates and CVV details through compromised websites, data breaches, phishing links or fake payment gateways. Compromised online platforms: If an online shopping website, payment gateway or merchant account is compromised, stored card information may be exposed.Similar Crime:One minute, three transactions: Man loses Rs 3.4LThree back-to-back transactions within a minute cost a 30-year-old private firm employee Rs 3.4 lakh after fraudsters misused his credit card, which he claimed he had not used for the last five months. He received alerts for all three transactions together while he was on a phone call on Nov 6. He immediately contacted the card support team and reported the fraud.Rehman (name changed) from Lingarajapura said the transactions included Rs 1,36,996 at Innovative Retail Concept (BigBasket), Rs 39,200 at Php Indus Appstore Private and Rs 1,64,852 at Blinkit.He said he had neither made nor approved the payments; he had not received or shared any OTP.How to stay safe*Disable international transactions: Keep international usage switched off unless required. Enable it only when making overseas payments.*Set transaction limits: Set lower spending limits for online, contactless and international transactions. Increase them temporarily when necessary.*Never share card details: Do not disclose your card number, CVV, expiry date, PIN or OTP to anyone, including people claiming to represent banks.*Avoid suspicious links: Do not click on links received through SMS, WhatsApp, emails or social media that promise rewards, refunds, credit card upgrades or fee waivers.*Do not install unknown APK files: Avoid downloading applications from unverified websites or links. articles.title: Temporal causa alagamentos em diversas ruas de Volta Redonda | G1
articles.standfirst: Forte chuva caiu nesta quinta-feira (19) no município.
articles.summary: Forte chuva caiu nesta quinta-feira (19) no município.
articles.body:
Um temporal atingiu Volta Redonda (RJ) na noite desta quinta-feira (19) e causou alagamentos em diferentes pontos da cidade. Foram registrados casos nos bairros Vila Santa Cecília, Santo Agostinho e Centro.

Imagens enviadas a produção da TV Rio Sul mostram ruas tomadas pela água durante a chuva. Em alguns locais, o volume de água dificultou a passagem de veículos e pedestres.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Defesa Civil, mas, até a publicação desta matéria, o boletim sobre a chuva ainda não havia sido concluído. Também não havia informações sobre feridos ou desalojados.

Temporal causa alagamentos em diversas ruas de Volta Redonda — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A orientação é para que moradores evitem transitar por áreas alagadas e procurem locais seguros durante períodos de chuva intensa.

Em caso de rajadas de vento: não se abrigue debaixo de árvores, pois há leve risco de queda e descargas elétricas e não estacione veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda.

Evite usar aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada.

Obtenha mais informações junto à Defesa Civil (telefone 199) e ao Corpo de Bombeiros (telefone 193).

articles.title: Will the Shenzhen summit safeguard world peace?
articles.summary: Xi, Putin and Trump issue ‘Peace Declaration’ after historic summit.
articles.body:
A three-way meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States has yielded a number of commitments.

Xi Jinping hosted Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in the city of Shenzhen, China on Thursday.

In a joint statement called a “Peace Declaration”, the three countries’ presidents pledged to safeguard international security and increase the production of refined petroleum products.

They also stressed that a nuclear war should never be fought because it cannot be won.

And they agreed to keep channels of dialogue open to resolve conflicts such as the war in Ukraine.

But how will Xi, Putin and Trump turn these commitments into actions?

articles.title: Caruaru acende luzes e inicia programação do Natal Iluminado 2026  | G1
articles.standfirst: Iluminação foi inaugurada nesta quinta-feira (19), na Estação Ferroviária, e ficará disponível para visitação até 6 de janeiro de 2027. Decoração inclui árvore de 18 metros e novos pontos de iluminação.
articles.summary: O Natal Iluminado Caruaru 2026 conta com 4 mil itens decorativos, árvore de 18 metros e atrações na zona rural e urbana que seguem disponíveis até janeiro de 2027.
articles.body:
A decoração do Caruaru , Natal Iluminado 2026 foi inaugurada nesta quinta-feira (19), com o acendimento das luzes da Estação Ferroviária. Ao todo, são cerca de 4 mil itens decorativos por diferentes pontos da cidade e também da zona rural de Caruaru, no Agreste de Pernambuco.

A programação de lançamento contou com apresentações culturais e o acendimento oficial da iluminação natalina. Entre os destaques estão uma árvore de Natal de 18 metros de altura, na Estação Ferroviária, e uma imagem de 10 metros na Praça do Rosário. A decoração poderá ser visitada até 6 de janeiro de 2027.

Além da Estação Ferroviária e da Praça do Rosário, outros espaços públicos receberam iluminação especial. No Monte Bom Jesus, por exemplo, também foram instaladas peças decorativas.

Uma das atrações é uma locomotiva que faz referência ao tradicional Trem do Forró, de Caruaru. A estrutura conta com um efeito de fumaça saindo da chaminé.

A iluminação natalina foi instalada em 21 localidades, entre bairros, praças e comunidades da zona rural. Quatro pontos recebem a decoração pela primeira vez: Terminal Rodoviário, Giradouro Indianópolis, Vila do Juá e Lajedo do Cedro.

Caruaru, Natal Iluminado 2026 — Foto: Jaira Lima

Avenida Agamenon Magalhães e Avenida Rio Branco

Caruaru, Natal Iluminado 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Jefferson Tetto

A estrutura montada na Estação Ferroviária também conta com espaços para comerciantes e ambulantes. O público encontra barracas de alimentação, com opções como pipoca, algodão-doce e chocolate quente, além de brinquedos para as crianças.

articles.title: Escala 5x2: Lula assina decreto e defende equilíbrio fiscal | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta quinta-feira (19), o presidente assinou decreto que regulamenta a jornada de trabalho 5x2. Novos critérios aumentam o valor da hora extra.
articles.summary: Lula assina decreto da escala 5x2 para reduzir a jornada de trabalho e reforça que ajuste fiscal não cortará direitos sociais.
articles.body:
O presidente Lula defendeu nesta quinta-feira (19) o compromisso com o ajuste das contas públicas. Ele assinou o decreto que regulamenta a jornada de trabalho 5x2.

O decreto regulamenta a redução da jornada de trabalho para 42 horas, distribuídas em cinco dias da semana. As regras passam a valer no dia 16 de dezembro de 2026. Com a redução da jornada, muda também o cálculo da hora extra. Na prática, as horas extras vão ficar mais caras, já que o valor é resultado da divisão do salário pelo número de horas trabalhadas.

Na semana que vem, o governo vai publicar portarias sobre o tema. De acordo com o Ministério do Trabalho , os dias de repouso não precisam ser necessariamente no sábado e no domingo. Acordos coletivos poderão definir as regras de compensação, desde que garantindo oito dias de descanso por mês.

O presidente Lula aproveitou a cerimônia para tratar de um assunto considerado prioritário pelo governo: o ajuste fiscal aprovado na quarta-feira (18) no Senado e que representa um impacto de até R$ 56 bilhões no Orçamento de 2027. O governo se esforça para aprovar a matéria na Câmara na semana que vem, mas vem enfrentando críticas. Alguns parlamentares da própria base consideram que haverá cortes em programas sociais.

Em cerimônia no Planalto, Lula declara compromisso com o equilíbrio das contas públicas — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Nesta quinta-feira (19), o presidente Lula disse que houve uma confusão sobre o assunto e que essa preocupação é fruto de falta de informação:

"Alguns companheiros, possivelmente por falta de informação completa, ou por falta de discussão, sabe, não entenderam. O dado concreto é o seguinte: enquanto eu for presidente da República, não haverá diminuição dos direitos que o povo brasileiro conquistou nesse país".

No mesmo discurso, Lula ressaltou o compromisso com o equilíbrio das contas e procurou negar que o pacote é resultado de pressões do mercado financeiro :

"Eu sei que muitas vezes o mercado reclama, muitas vezes o mercado também está interessado, sabe, em fazer as reivindicações dele. O mercado quer que a gente tenha um controle fiscal, mas não é o mercado que deseja o controle fiscal. Quem deseja o controle fiscal sou eu. Quem deseja a economia séria sou eu. Quem tem que ter responsabilidade fiscal é o governo. E nós já temos muita experiência para mostrar que nós temos responsabilidade fiscal nesse país".

articles.title: Cacique Raoni: Lula visita líder em MT e assina demarcação de terra | G1
articles.standfirst: O cacique de 94 anos está recebendo cuidados paliativos desde setembro, após o diagnóstico de câncer no aparelho digestivo.
articles.summary: Em visita ao cacique Raoni, que está em cuidados paliativos, o presidente Lula assinou a portaria de posse permanente da Terra Indígena Kapôt Nhinore, em Mato Grosso.
articles.body:
Depois de cerimônia no Palácio do Planalto, o presidente Lula viajou para Mato Grosso, onde visitou o cacique Raoni .

Uma casa em Peixoto de Azevedo é onde o cacique Raoni Metuktire, de 94 anos, está recebendo cuidados paliativos desde setembro, após o diagnóstico de câncer no aparelho digestivo. Raoni é uma das lideranças indígenas mais respeitadas no Brasil e reconhecido internacionalmente.

A visita, de meia hora, foi reservada, sem a presença da imprensa. De lá, Lula seguiu até a sede do Instituto Raoni, onde assinou a portaria que declara a posse permanente dos povos indígenas à Terra Indígena Kapôt Nhinore. A busca pela demarcação faz parte da luta de Raoni ao longo dos anos.

“Essa é uma coisa que eu agradeço a Deus. O Raoni é o indígena vivo que melhor representa a tradição indígena desse país”, afirma o presidente Lula.

Presidente Lula viajou para Mato Grosso, onde visitou o cacique Raoni — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A região de 362 mil hectares, entre os estados de Mato Grosso e do Pará, fica na transição entre o Cerrado e a Floresta Amazônica, ao lado do Parque Indígena do Xingu. A área é alvo de disputas entre indígenas e produtores rurais há mais de quatro décadas.

Ao todo, o processo de demarcação de um território indígena tem que passar por sete etapas. A primeira, de identificação e delimitação da área, já foi concluída pela Funai em 2003. A assinatura da portaria, nesta quinta-feira (19), é a terceira etapa. Até o registro final, ainda faltam: a demarcação física, a retirada dos não indígenas, a homologação presidencial e, por fim, a incorporação ao patrimônio da União.

articles.title: ‘Amava crianças’, diz irmã de professora que morreu em acidente no AC | G1
articles.standfirst: Ciliane Silva morreu na noite da última terça-feira (17). Ela seguia de motocicleta pela rodovia, em Cruzeiro do Sul, quando colidiu com o animal. Irmã lamentou a morte.
articles.summary: Ciliane Silva morreu na noite da última terça-feira (17). Ela seguia de motocicleta pela rodovia, em Cruzeiro do Sul, quando colidiu com o animal. Irmã lamentou a morte.
articles.body:
A afirmação é de Ciane Silva, irmã da professora Ciliane Silva, de 31 anos, que morreu na noite de terça-feira (17) após colidir a motocicleta contra um búfalo solto na BR-364 , em Cruzeiro do Sul , interior do Acre.

A professora foi sepultada nessa quarta (18). Familiares e amigos se reuniram para dar o último adeus e soltaram balões para homenagear a professora. ( Veja o vídeo acima )

Ao g1 , Ciane contou que a irmã era uma pessoa prestativa e fazia o que podia para ajudar as pessoas. Segundo ela, Ciliane trabalhava desde 2021 e sustentava os dois filhos, um de 13 e outro de 12 anos, sozinha.

“A minha irmã fazia de tudo, era uma pessoa que não negava nada a ninguém, o que ela podia fazer, fazia. Era professora mesmo, [...] formada em pedagogia e em educação física, a minha irmã tinha tudo”, contou.

Ciliane Silva, de 31 anos, morreu após colidir a moto contra um búfalo na BR-364, em Cruzeiro do Sul — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Conforme Ciane, no dia do acidente, a irmã passou a manhã com a família e estava feliz. Após o encontro, ela foi trabalhar normalmente e, ao retornar para casa, ocorreu a colisão na rodovia.

Ciliane era pedagoga e trabalhava como professora na Escola Cora Coralina, localizada na região da BR-364. Ela morava na Vila Liberdade, zona rural de Cruzeiro do Sul.

Ainda de acordo com a irmã, a professora gostava de crianças e de atuar na área. “Trabalhava nessa área porque gostava. Uma coisa que gostava era trabalhar com criança, trabalhou no EJA também, mas disse que a criança era a área dela. Sempre gostou mais de criança”, afirmou.

Segundo Ciane, o dono do búfalo não foi identificado e o pai dela registrou um boletim de ocorrência em uma delegacia para que a pessoa seja responsabilizada.

Ciliane e Ciane se formaram juntas a outra irmã no Acre — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

“Tudo que a minha irmã queria, ela conseguia. Tinha uma fé tão grande em Deus. Tinha tirado a habitação dela, a D, e estava tão feliz mostrando [...], para dirigir micro-ônibus”, disse.

Além da graduação em pedagogia, Ciliane também era formada em educação física. Em outubro do ano passado, ela e as irmãs concluíram o ensino superior e se formararm juntas.

“A última que ela se formou. A primeira graduação estava só, essa a gente fez juntas. [...] Só nos formamos juntas, porque ela era uma área e nós éramos de outra”, explicou.

Após a colisão, a professora foi encontrada em estado grave e encaminhada ao hospital da Vila Santa Luzia, onde sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória. As equipes médicas fizeram procedimentos de reanimação, mas ela não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu na unidade de saúde.

Segundo o médico do Samu, Miguel Washing, a equipe de suporte básico de Santa Luzia foi enviada inicialmente ao local por estar mais próxima da ocorrência. Segundo ele, a vítima apresentava sinais de traumas graves na cabeça e no abdômen.

Ao chegar à unidade de saúde, Ciliane sofreu uma parada cardiorrespiratória (PCR). Uma equipe de suporte avançado também foi deslocada para auxiliar no atendimento, mas não conseguiu reverter o quadro.

"O quadro dela já era bastante grave quando a equipe chegou. A gente identificou, provavelmente, um traumatismo cranioencefálico grave e também um comprometimento importante na região abdominal. Quando ela chegou à unidade de Santa Luzia, teve uma parada cardiorrespiratória e foram iniciados todos os procedimentos para tentar reverter essa situação. Infelizmente, não houve êxito nas tentativas de reanimação", relatou.

O médico também explicou que a gravidade das lesões encontradas pela equipe indicava um quadro bastante delicado devido à extensão dos ferimentos.

articles.title: Fiona, hipopótamo famoso nas redes, morre após engolir gorro | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal de 9 anos ficou sob cuidados veterinários por vários dias. Equipe tentou colonoscopia, ultrassom e até uma plataforma de vibração para ajudar na eliminação do objeto.
articles.summary: Animal de 9 anos ficou sob cuidados veterinários por vários dias após ingerir o objeto. Equipe tentou colonoscopia, ultrassom e até uma plataforma de vibração.
articles.body:
A hipopótamo Fiona engoliu um gorro e, agora, veterinários vão usar uma plataforma vibratória para ajudá-la a expelir o item. — Foto: John Minchillo/AP

Fiona, o hipopótamo-fêmea que se tornou uma das principais atrações do Zoológico de Cincinnati , nos Estados Unidos, morreu nesta quinta-feira (19), aos 9 anos , após complicações causadas pela ingestão de um gorro de tricô .

O objeto caiu acidentalmente no recinto do animal cerca de 11 dias atrás .

Segundo o zoológico, um visitante jogou o gorro para o alto , ele foi atingido por um ventilador de teto e acabou lançado para dentro da área onde Fiona estava.

Depois de engolir o objeto, Fiona passou a ser acompanhada 24 horas por dia pela equipe veterinária. Nos dias seguintes, começou a apresentar perda de apetite.

Os veterinários tentaram diferentes procedimentos para ajudar o gorro a passar pelo sistema digestivo.

Fiona foi submetida a ultrassom e colonoscopia, e a equipe do zoo também chegou a usar uma plataforma de vibração emprestada de uma fazenda na tentativa de estimular o funcionamento do intestino.

Uma cirurgia foi descartada por ser considerada arriscada demais para um hipopótamo adulto. Fiona pesava mais de uma tonelada , e os especialistas também tinham dificuldade para determinar exatamente onde o gorro estava no sistema digestivo.

O zoológico informou que a equipe tentou várias formas de ajudá-la, mas o quadro evoluiu para uma emergência médica.

Fiona ganhou fama mundial depois de nascer seis semanas antes do previsto, em 2017, pesando apenas 13,2 kg — muito abaixo do peso esperado para um hipopótamo recém-nascido.

Ela não conseguia mamar sozinha e precisou receber cuidados intensivos da equipe do zoológico. Sua recuperação passou a ser acompanhada por milhões de pessoas nas redes sociais e transformou Fiona em uma das figuras mais conhecidas do local.

Ao longo dos anos, sua imagem apareceu em livros, produtos e campanhas do zoológico, e ela se tornou uma atração para visitantes de várias partes dos Estados Unidos.

articles.summary: O prêmio para o ganhador da edição desta quinta-feira era de R$ 37,7 milhões.
articles.body:
O sorteio do concurso 3.088 da Mega-Sena foi realizado na noite desta quinta-feira (19), em São Paulo. O prêmio para as apostas que acertassem as seis dezenas era de R$ 37,7 milhões . No entanto, ninguém levou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou para R$ 45 milhões .

articles.title: An 82-year-old Arkansas man lived on his family's 331 acres for over 30 years, but relatives sought a sale; an appeals court later dismissed his challenge
articles.summary: An 82-year-old Arkansas man who had lived on his family's 331-acre property for more than three decades could not obtain a reversal of its court-ordered
articles.body: An 82-year-old Arkansas man who had lived on his family's 331-acre property for more than three decades could not obtain a reversal of its court-ordered sale after the land was transferred to a third-party buyer. The dispute involved inherited property shared by relatives, with some family members seeking to sell the land while William J “Bud” Cooper wanted it divided among the co-owners so he could continue living there.In a November 18, 2026, decision available on Justia, the Arkansas Court of Appeals dismissed Cooper's appeal, ruling that the dispute had become moot because the property had already been sold and its title transferred. Although the majority did not decide the merits of his challenge to the partition order, two judges dissented, arguing that the lower court had committed reversible error and that Cooper had been deprived of his opportunity to obtain meaningful appellate review.A family inheritance became a property disputeThe case concerned 331 acres near Boswell in Izard County, Arkansas. The property included pastureland, timberland, hills, creek and river-bottom areas, approximately 400 feet of frontage along the White River and seven platted town lots. The land originally belonged to Sylvester Smith, who died without a will in 1956. It subsequently passed to his three daughters. One daughter had no children, while the other two had descendants who became the Cooper and Bridgman families.By the time the legal dispute began, the Coopers collectively owned one-third of the property, while Stephanie Ann and Gary Alan Bridgman held the remaining two-thirds as tenants in common. In 2017, the Bridgmans filed a partition action seeking to have the property divided or sold if it could not be divided without substantial harm to the co-owners.Cooper and his sisters opposed the action. They claimed exclusive ownership through adverse possession and argued that the Bridgmans' long delay in seeking partition should prevent them from obtaining a sale under the legal doctrine of laches. Cooper also wanted the land divided physically rather than sold, allowing the family members to receive separate portions according to their ownership interests.Why the court ordered the 331 acres soldAfter several hearings, the Izard County Circuit Court rejected the Coopers' claims of adverse possession and laches and granted the Bridgmans' partition petition. The court later rejected the Coopers' request for a division in kind, meaning a physical division of the land among the owners. Instead, it ordered an open-market sale through a real estate broker.However, the Arkansas Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act requires a court to find that property cannot be divided in kind without great prejudice to the co-owners as a group before ordering a sale. The circuit court did not expressly make that required finding. The property was privately sold to a third party on February 5, 2025. The circuit court confirmed the sale on February 13 and subsequently authorised the distribution of the proceeds, with one-third going to the Coopers and two-thirds to the Bridgmans after outstanding debts were addressed.Cooper appealed the confirmation order, arguing that the court had failed to follow the statutory requirements before ordering the sale. He wanted the decision reversed and the case sent back for further proceedings to determine whether the land could be divided physically.Appeals court dismisses the case as mootThe Arkansas Court of Appeals focused on what it could legally do after the sale had been completed. By the time the appeal was considered, the property had been transferred to a third-party purchaser who was not involved in the litigation. The court explained that it could not undo the transaction or return the land to Cooper.The majority therefore concluded that the appeal had become moot. It also noted that Cooper had not asked for monetary relief or challenged how the sale proceeds were divided. His requested remedy was to have the property returned for a possible physical division. Two judges, Barrett and Hixson, disagreed with the dismissal. In a dissenting opinion, Hixson argued that the circuit court had clearly failed to make the mandatory finding required under the Heirs Property Act before ordering a sale.He also criticised the appeals court for allowing the sale proceeds to be distributed while the appeal was pending and then dismissing the case because the dispute had become moot. He argued that the court could have reversed the decision and allowed the circuit court to consider whether another remedy was possible.The appeal was ultimately dismissed, leaving the completed sale undisturbed. The decision did not resolve whether the original partition order complied with the statutory requirements, but it highlighted the difficulties heirs can face when challenging the sale of inherited family property.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chilling bus video shows Brooklyn apartment building crumble in seconds
articles.summary: Newly released Metropolitan Transportation Authority bus video captures the moment a Flatbush building collapsed into a construction pit, killing eight.
articles.body: Newly released surveillance video from a passing Metropolitan Transportation Authority bus captures the moment a three-story Brooklyn apartment building collapsed last week, killing eight people and injuring 18 others. The video shows the mixed-use building, built in the 1930s, collapsing into an adjacent construction pit around 4 p.m. ET Nov. 11, at 1321 Flatbush Ave. in the city's Flatbush neighborhood. As the building collapsed, a thick cloud of dust engulfed the block, exposing interior rooms in a neighboring building. NYC BUILDING COLLAPSE: EIGHT BODIES RECOVERED AS FIRST RESPONDERS SEARCH FOR SURVIVORS New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that six adults and two children, ages 9 and 10, were killed, and 18 others were injured. Six victims died on the property, while two died at nearby hospitals, officials said. The NYPD identified the deceased as Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9; Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10; Gabriel Siguencia, 22; Barry Mamadou, 23; Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26; Edgar Sapon, 26; Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31; and Ndiaye Mamadou, 31. At least two of those killed were construction workers at the adjacent 2625 Bedford Ave. site, Mamdani said. AT LEAST 2 DEAD, 17 INJURED AFTER NYC BUILDING COLLAPSE The Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office, the NYPD and the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) have launched a joint investigation into the collapse and will attempt to determine whether the excavation site had adequate supports to prevent surrounding buildings from shifting. DOB records show inspectors issued a stop-work order and a $2,500 fine at 2625 Bedford Ave. in March for inadequate overhead protection during demolition. In April, inspectors issued a Class 1 violation and a $10,000 fine after demolition resumed despite the order. The city allowed work to resume in May after the violations were corrected. The architect, property owner and general contractor identified in city records did not respond to Fox News Digital's prior requests for comment. articles.title: Why are Bukele’s Salvadoran troops in Haiti and what have they achieved?
articles.summary: With crowds rallying behind El Salvador’s deployment in Haiti, analysts question whether civilians are any safer.
articles.body:
The streets of Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince, rang out on Tuesday and Wednesday with chants from local residents in support of a president who was not their own: El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele. In a country where the scars of foreign intervention run deep, some Haitians are placing their hopes on another foreign force, this time from El Salvador, to help take their neighbourhoods back from armed gangs.

Thousands turned out to cheer on the roughly 2,500 soldiers Bukele has sent since October. What began as a narrow mission to rescue four missing Salvadoran aviation technicians has grown into a much broader military operation.

For some of those who marched, the intervention is exactly what the country needs after years of kidnappings, killings, and displacement, with little sign of relief.

But even with the Haitian government’s backing and a warm reception from the public, questions are growing about what the troops are doing on the ground and what kind of mark Bukele will ultimately leave on Haiti.

The immediate trigger came on October 18, when four Salvadoran aviation technicians working with the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) went missing after armed men attacked their vehicle near Port-au-Prince.

The force was created to help Haitian authorities deal with a security crisis that has grown more severe since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise. According to Reuters, gangs now control more than 80 percent of the capital region, with Haitian and international forces struggling to reclaim that territory.

Shortly after the technicians went missing, Bukele announced a new military operation in Haiti, sending 100 special forces soldiers to rescue them. Since then, he’s sent about 2,500 in total.

Most of them are operating outside the UN-backed force and outside the UN support office’s monitoring mechanisms, according to UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric .

And the deployment itself has turned from a narrow rescue operation to a broader offensive against Haiti’s gangs, with Salvadoran soldiers joining Haitian security forces, the GSF, and private contractors, including Blackwater founder Erik Prince’s Vectus Global.

Bukele, who gained international notoriety for a crackdown on gangs in El Salvador that led to a sharp decline in crime but has drawn widespread condemnation over human rights abuses, has been aggressively promoting the deployment on social media.

He has posted dramatic videos of helicopter attacks on gang leaders’ properties and, more recently, footage of rallies cheering on his troops.

“I never expected anything like this,” he wrote in a Tuesday post accompanying a video of a rally. “I hear you loud and clear. I love you, too.”

Neither the Haitian government nor the Salvadoran government replied to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment about the troops in Haiti.

Why are some Haitians cheering on the Salvadoran troops?

The troops have landed amid a worsening humanitarian crisis in Haiti, with nearly 1.5 million people displaced from their homes, and violence making it difficult to access food and basic services. More than 22,000 people have been killed in gang-related violence, including security operations, since 2022, according to Reuters.

At rallies in Port-au-Prince and other parts of Haiti, demonstrators voiced support for the deployment. Some who spoke to The Associated Press news agency described losing loved ones to gang violence and being forced to leave their homes.

“The support we see from many Haitians comes from sheer desperation after years of failure and widespread terror,” Louimann Maceus, president of the human rights organisation Ensemble des Citoyens Competents a la Recherche de l’Egalite des Droits de l’Homme en Haiti (ECCREDHH), told Al Jazeera. “People are exhausted.”

“There is a genuine hope, especially among the hundreds of thousands of internally displaced people we work with who just want to return safely home,” said Maceus, who lives in Port-au-Prince.

That hope, he said, follows years of frustration with UN-backed forces, which he said had done little to improve security.

The Salvadoran deployment already outnumbers the GSF, according to numbers from the GSF’s special representative Jack Christofides, on October 18, when it had just surpassed 2,000 personnel.

International Crisis Group analyst Diego Da Rin also links some of the enthusiasm to what he describes as a really effective communication campaign by Bukele, whose videos of strikes on gang leaders’ homes are all over Haitian social media.

“These are symbolic wins that everybody was waiting for,” he said, adding that AI-generated videos were also circulating of gang leaders being arrested.

But support for the deployment is not universal. Da Rin pointed to the residents of gang-controlled areas.

“Many of these people, who clearly see the risks in these iron-fist operations, are extremely scared of being attacked and being collateral damage of any of these operations,” said Da Rin.

What have Salvadoran troops actually achieved?

Security force clashes and drone strikes targeting gangs increased by 46 percent in the 21 days after the start of the deployment, compared to the 21 days before it, according to the conflict monitoring group the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED).

ACLED estimated more than 100 people were killed in the same period, including at least 26 civilians.

Haiti’s Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier, however, said on Monday that the government had received no reports of civilian casualties in the latest operations, which it described as professional, according to Reuters.

Bukele has used social media to highlight what he sees as the offensive’s successes.

After Salvadoran troops joined Haitian police and a government task force in a November 8 attack on a house belonging to Wilson Joseph, leader of the powerful 400 Mawozo gang, Bukele posted video of helicopters repeatedly firing at the building, as people ran away from the area.

Joseph reportedly was not there and survived the attack.

A few days later, Haitian national police and Bukele announced that they’d retaken control of the national football stadium. Bukele shared video of robot dogs armed with rifles moving through the corridors of the stadium alongside troops, although it’s unclear how exactly they were used in the operation.

Da Rin said it was worth noting that police initially credited their officers and the task force with retaking the stadium before handing control over to Salvadoran troops, who set up a base there.

The stadium is a useful spot to launch operations against nearby gang strongholds, he added, but it represented a relatively small gain from positions Haitian forces had already secured.

On Wednesday, Bukele posted another video showing a helicopter attack on the home of Jeff Larose, leader of the Taliban gang, which controls the area of Canaan in northern Port-au-Prince.

It was not clear whether the attack had killed Larose or whether Haiti’s police or army had participated. The GSF was not involved, according to The Associated Press.

For displaced people looking to return home, the gains have yet to make a tangible difference, said Da Rin.

After the attack on Joseph’s house, none of the security forces set up a permanent presence in the area, he said.

“Armed groups were able to return and are now intimidating residents, searching their phones, threatening people suspected of sharing information with the security forces,” Da Rin told Al Jazeera.

He warned that forces appeared to be “in a race” to show results without a unified strategy to sustain them.

Salvadoran officials have said they plan to leave once the missing technicians are found. Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, told the Associated Press earlier this month that they were dead, but their fate remains officially unknown.

“The priority should be to plan the most difficult part, how the forces will work together to establish lasting control,” said Da Rin.

Why are some experts concerned about the deployment?

The terms of the Salvadoran deployment haven’t been made public.

Amnesty International has called on both governments to explain who oversees the troops, what rules govern their use of force, and how civilians can safely report abuses.

On Monday, Salvadoran Vice President Felix Ulloa said the agreement would be kept under wraps until diplomatic conditions allowed its release and accused critics of having a “hidden agenda”.

Sam Vigersky, a fellow with the Council on Foreign Relations who studies emergency relief in response to armed conflict, said the lack of monitoring or publicly shared rules of engagement for Salvadoran troops operating outside the GSF means “we do not know what collateral damage might come of these offensives”.

For Vigersky, the lesson from past interventions, including a UN peacekeeping mission whose personnel brought cholera to Haiti and were implicated in widespread sexual abuse, is that “oversight matters”.

“Absent that,” he said, “the deep scars that Haiti has already from these past UN or other operations are only likely to grow.”

articles.title: US appeals court lets Trump end TPS deportation protections for Venezuelans
articles.summary: The appeals court’s ruling prevents a lower-court decision from taking effect, which would block Trump from lifting TPS.
articles.body:
A United States appeals court has allowed the administration of President Donald Trump to move forward for now with the removal of deportation protections for Venezuelans .

The ruling on Wednesday cancels out a previous order by a lower-court judge that required the government to restore the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) of Venezuelans, which shields recipients against deportation.

The effort to end the TPS protections has proceeded despite humanitarian concerns .

Since taking office for a second term, Trump has sought to carry out what he calls the largest deportation effort in US history. Part of that agenda has been to roll back programmes like TPS.

But in September 2025, US District Judge Edward Chen blocked the expiration of TPS protections for Venezuelans, arguing that deporting those individuals would put them in harm’s way.

He also ruled that the Trump administration had overstepped its authority by seeking to shorten TPS extensions granted under the preceding president, Joe Biden. Such decisions, Chen added, needed to be taken with “careful study and analysis”.

Some 600,000 Venezuelans in the US were protected under TPS programmes.

The Supreme Court paused Chen’s ruling in October 2025. But that pause expired this month, and Chen’s order was set to take effect on Friday.

On Wednesday, the Trump administration filed an emergency request to the Supreme Court to extend the pause before Thursday’s appeals court ruling.

The appeals court’s decision does not nix the ongoing legal challenges to Trump’s efforts to revoke TPS extensions. But it allows the administration to suspend deportation protections while the challenges make their way through court.

The Trump administration has sought to strip large numbers of immigrants of their legal protections in a bid to render them deportable. Other programmes, like humanitarian parole, have also come under the administration’s scrutiny.

TPS allows foreign nationals already in the US to remain while conditions in their home countries are too dangerous or unstable to return to.

Humanitarian parole, meanwhile, allows people outside the US to come in on a temporary basis, often to escape similarly perilous conditions.

The Trump administration has argued that TPS designations are meant to be temporary — and that previous presidencies extended such protections without cause.

It has also maintained that conditions have improved in places like Venezuela, where a US military action on January 3 resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro.

Human rights advocates, however, have noted that Maduro’s government remains largely intact. That leadership has been accused of abuses ranging from arbitrary imprisonment to the torture of political dissidents.

The US Department of State currently warns against travel to Venezuela, citing issues such as crime, kidnapping and poor health infrastructure.

articles.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
articles.summary: Fiona, who became an internet star after her premature birth in 2017, "fought until she couldn’t anymore", the zoo says.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona has died just days after swallowing a knitted hat that slipped into her enclosure.

"It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said on Thursday afternoon.

Fiona, who became a social media star after her premature birth in 2017, swallowed the hat about 10 days ago and required emergency care.

The vet staff "tried everything they could to help her" but "it was ultimately too much to overcome", the zoo said.

"We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, had said that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.

While she seemed fine at first, her appetite started to decrease a few days later, and the zoo staff tried to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

An ultrasound before her death showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine. A zookeeper said surgery was not an option for full-grown hippos and "our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own".

The zoo also tried a different approach to attempt to get the hat to pass by encouraging Fiona to stand on a vibration plate platform borrowed from a local horse farm.

"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Jenike said.

Fiona was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017 and at first struggled to survive. At birth, she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

Her death is also very premature, with hippos normally living up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.

"Although this was not an intentional incident, of which, regrettably, there are many, Fiona's painful death is a tragic reminder that everyone should behave carefully and respectfully around animals," Debbie Metzler, the Managing Director of Captive Wildlife for the animal rights group Peta.

"Peta expects that the zoo will review its protocols to help prevent anything like this from happening again, and we urge every visitor to secure their belongings and never toss objects near an animal's enclosure."

As well as being famous online, Fiona's story inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval said Fiona "was a symbol of perseverance and joy" in the city.

"She brought smiles to so many faces, from kids to parents to visitors from around the world," he wrote on X. "Our city is heartbroken, but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole."

articles.title: Haiti police say at least 34 suspected gang members killed in raid
articles.summary: Police say the raid targeted the Martissant area, located on a key route out of Port-au-Prince held by gangs since 2021.
articles.body:
At least 34 suspected gang members were killed in a police operation in Martissant, a neighbourhood in Haiti’s capital that has been under gang control for more than five years, Haitian police said.

Haiti’s National Police, which posted footage of armoured vehicles moving through the neighbourhood, said their officers carried out the raid on Thursday with an anti-gang task force that includes personnel from Vectus Global, the private security firm founded by Blackwater founder Erik Prince.

Police reported no other casualties and said none of the roughly 2,500 Salvadoran troops in Haiti took part.

The Martissant neighbourhood is located along a key road that connects Port-au-Prince to Haiti’s western and southern cities, and was used by thousands of people daily before rival gangs began fighting to control the area in 2021.

The subsequent violence forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes, according to a July 2022 UN report.

Armed groups have since demanded payment for using the road or shot at cars that have tried to pass through, making it difficult to bring goods in and out of the city.

Separately, the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force said it was stepping up operations in Tabarre after months of night patrols and efforts to identify gang positions.

“The objective is clear: not just to displace gangs, but to dismantle their hold on communities, reclaim territory, and prevent their return,” the force said on X.

In the central Artibonite region, the force said their troops had come under fire while clearing barricades and filling in trenches that gangs had dug along National Route 5, north of the town of Gros-Morne.

“During the operation, gang members opened fire on GSF personnel, who responded and forced them to withdraw,” said the update on X.

The raid in Martissant comes as Salvadoran troops have been carrying out joint operations with Haitian police. El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele initially sent troops to search for four Salvadoran aviation technicians who went missing after an October 18 ambush near Port-au-Prince.

What began as a search for the missing men has since grown into a broader offensive against Haiti’s gangs.

articles.title: At 11, Rob Adams lived in a truck until a Texas family offered his family a home stocked with food for Christmas; decades later, his Thanksgiving charity has delivered more than 29,000 meals across nine US cities
articles.summary: At 11 years old, Rob Adams lived in a truck with his family until a Texas family offered them a home stocked with food for Christmas.
articles.body: At 11 years old, Rob Adams lived in a truck with his family until a Texas family offered them a home stocked with food for Christmas. articles.title: ‘Stand your ground’ claim falters in road rage killing as men charged with murder, ex-cops face accusations
articles.summary: Two South Carolina men face murder charges in Scott Spivey's road rage death after his sister uncovered recordings that sank their "stand your ground" defense.
articles.body: Two South Carolina men have been charged with murder in the road rage shooting death of a man whose sister uncovered evidence that the slaying was not self-defense as originally claimed. And two former police officers involved in the investigation are facing accusations of official misconduct. Scott Spivey, a 33-year-old insurance adjuster from North Carolina, died Sept. 9, 2023, after a car chase on Highway 9 in Horry County led to his shooting death on Camp Swamp Road, 9 miles away. Charles "Weldon" Boyd and Kenneth "Bradley" Williams had originally invoked the state's "stand your ground" law and argued they were defending themselves from an irrational driver. They were both arrested Wednesday, more than three years after the incident. SECRET TAPES SINK SHOOTER'S DEFENSE IN SCOTT SPIVEY ROAD RAGE KILLING Brandon Strickland and Paul Vescovi, a former deputy chief and sergeant with the Horry County Police Department, also face charges, including misconduct in office and obstruction of justice, according to local reports. Strickland, who allegedly spoke with Boyd on the phone after the shooting, was also charged with criminal conspiracy. All four made initial appearances in criminal court Thursday afternoon. The judge did not rule on their bond requests at the end of the two-hour hearing, according to the Myrtle Beach-based WMBF-TV. Separate decisions were expected to be posted later. At the time of the shooting, Spivey, Boyd and Williams were all armed, according to court documents. Spivey eventually pulled over, got out of his vehicle and screamed at Boyd and Williams to stop following him. The pursuers allegedly opened fire and killed him in what his sister's attorney described as "a hail of gunfire" in a wrongful death lawsuit. WATCH: Investigative journalist discusses 'damning' recordings after road rage shooting Spivey's sister, Jennifer Spivey Foley, uncovered recordings from Boyd's phone buried in the police case file that had previously not been made public or factored into the case, and The Wall Street Journal published them last year, bringing national attention to the case. Foley attended the hearing Thursday and asked the judge to deny bond for both Boyd and Williams and to order a mental health evaluation for Boyd. According to court documents in the Spivey family's wrongful death case, the recordings indicate that Boyd told a 911 dispatcher that Spivey was "trying to get away" and nevertheless was prepared for a shootout. "If I see the gun again, I'm going to take the motherf----- down," Boyd allegedly told the dispatcher, according to the civil complaint in a wrongful death lawsuit filed in 2024. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Boyd remained on the line until the shooting took place, according to the wrongful death lawsuit. Read the wrongful death lawsuit: Later, according to the Journal report, he allegedly called his friend, who was Horry County's deputy police chief at the time. Defense filings in the civil case allege that Spivey had pointed a pistol at Williams' head and ran Boyd's truck off the road at the start of the encounter. In a 911 call, a man identified as Boyd told the dispatcher that the other driver shot first. O’Bryan Martin, an attorney for Williams, disputed the idea that the shooting was anything other than self-defense. In court documents in the civil case, lawyers for Boyd and Williams have accused Spivey of being the aggressor by pointing a gun at Williams through the window without provocation. Martin said that other drivers called 911 to report similarly erratic behavior before Spivey ran into Boyd’s truck on the highway. "When you're claiming self-defense, we always have to analyze, first and foremost: Well, who brought on the difficulty? Who caused this to start? Who started the fight, to boil it down? And if you've got any part in starting the fight, you can't then turn around and claim self-defense," Martin told Fox News Digital. "In this particular case, Scott Spivey set all this into motion." Martin also pointed to autopsy findings showing Spivey had a 0.13 blood alcohol content. "For over three years, Scott Spivey’s family has fought for something that should never have required a fight — the truth about how and why Scott was killed," Mark Tinsley, the attorney representing the victim's family, wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. articles.title: Comedian Heather McMahan doesn’t joke around when it comes to her cheese, lashes and these other travel must-haves
articles.summary: Comedian Heather McMahan is going on tour in 2027. She’s not traveling without her favorite packing cubes, snacks, lashes and compression socks.
articles.body: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. One of the things Heather McMahan has become an expert in throughout her career as a comedian is traveling. I know that might not totally make sense at first, but when you look at her 2027 schedule alone, you get it. Her Burning Down the House Tour is taking her across the country starting in January, she’s hosting her Absolutely Knot Cruise in May from Miami to the Bahamas, and somehow between all of that, she’s also recording her podcast and making it back home to Atlanta as much as possible. McMahan has packing, flying and on-the-go glam down to a science, and turning a hotel room into a home is her specialty. Because she’s such a travel professional, McMahan recently partnered with Hilton to debut its New Ways to Stay campaign, which included a pop-up experience in New York City’s Time Square and a vacation sweepstakes that sent six people on surprise solo getaways. I got to talk to McMahan at the pop-up, who told me that while there’s numerous luxury amenities at Hilton locations worldwide, there’s one she looks forward to the most. “I know you’re expecting me to say a nice gym,” she joked, “but I actually love that perfect 5 p.m. happy hour moment where you’re sitting in a great cocktail bar in a gorgeous hotel and you’re having your aperol spritz or whatever your drink of choice is — even if it’s a Diet Coke with a lime in it. You’re sitting there and you’re like, ‘We’re here. We arrived. Look at all the things we’ve done in this brand-new city or destination that we’ve been in today.’” McMahan also gave me a rundown of her travel essentials, including the top four things she brings for her dressing room while she’s on tour. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. “When I’m packing, I have every intention of keeping things organized. It’s all in the cubes, and then my husband calls me Hurricane Heather because when I get to a hotel, everything explodes out of my bag,” says McMahan. “He’s like, ‘Heather, this is the most organized chaos.’ But I know where my stuff is. It’s in the bags, that are in the other bags, that are in the cubes, that are shoved somewhere. Just don’t touch it.” If there’s one thing McMahan will admit to over-packing, it’s underwear. “Listen, I’m going to tell you right now: pack more underwear than you think, alright? Just grab a handful and at least throw an extra 10 in there because you never know,” she says. “But whatever you forgot at home, Hilton’s got it, so call down to the front desk, and be like, “Hi, I need a toothbrush kit.” Come on — they’re thinking three steps ahead. You think this is their first rodeo? They know what’s going on.” “I like to look nice on an airplane, so I’m always going to have a nice jacket, a blazer or a cashmere sweater,” says McMahan. “It’s freezing on airplanes, so it’s a way to kind of pull yourself together. You can have sweats on underneath, but just have a nice blazer or cashmere sweater.” One of her favorite sweaters to throw on is Spanx’s AirEssentials Half Zip, which is made from lightweight, silky-soft fabric to keep her cozy. McMahan also always wears compression socks to help with circulation on an airplane, especially because she often flies multiple times a week. She loves All in Motion’s Women’s Essential Compression Socks from Target, which comes in a two pack. They’re lightly cushioned, extend up to the knees and have a wide cuff, making them easy to put on and take off. There’s built-in arch support, too. “I’m one of those people who has every intention to download a movie or a new show on my iPad before I get on a flight, but I am just scrolling on TikTok for seven and a half hours while I fly to Istanbul. That’s just what I do,” says McMahan. She’s low maintenance about her in-flight entertainment, but she doesn’t mess around when it comes to snacks. “You do not want to see me panicking if you think my blood sugar has gotten low, so I’ve always got some sort of sweet treat and a protein snack,” says McMahan. Her two go-tos are Unreal’s Dark Chocolate Coconut Bars and Barebells’ Salty Peanut Protein Bars. But she has a savory favorite that she also can’t live without: “If you travel around with a hunk of parmigiano reggio cheese, you’re good to go,” says McMahan. “Just a little health tip: have a hunk of cheese in your back pocket.” “I’m pretty easy backstage,” says McMahan when I asked her about her pre-show routine. “I need quiet time before a show. I like to decompress before I turn it on, so I listen to a very specific Spotify playlist called ‘Cocktail Jazz.’ Then I do a full glam beat, and then I eat a hunk of cheese and a handful of salami, and chug a Spindrift — that’s what I do before a show. It’s really not that exciting or glamorous. It’s just a little salami, a little cheese and a glam beat. That’s all you need.” Speaking of her glam, McMahan says the number one most important part of it is her lashes, whether she’s going on stage or running errands at home. “I am wildly dedicated to Ardell Lashes,” she says. “I can put these on literally with my eyes closed or on the back of a jet ski. I wear Ardell’s 420s, 421s and 424s. I don’t leave the house without a lash.” Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who leads our Talking Shop series, interviewing people like Paris Hilton, Maureen Kelly, Lindsay Hubbard and Chase Crawford. To write this article, I talked to comedian Heather McMahan about her favorite travel essentials, especially when she’s on tour, and her partnership with Hilton. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Judge finds Thomas Markle mentally fit to stand trial on child abuse charges
articles.summary: Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse was deemed competent after an evaluation by a court-appointed psychiatrist.
articles.body:
A judge in Florida has declared Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, to be mentally competent to stand trial for possessing indecent images of children.

The hearing came after an evaluation by a court-appointed psychiatrist conducted on Prince Harry's 82-year-old father-in-law.

Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was ordered to stay in jail pending trial earlier this month after allegedly removing a location monitoring device.

The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November at an elderly care home that specialises in dementia. His arrest came after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles uncovered the abuse material.

Markle appeared in court in Tampa in a wheelchair, and his lawyers did not dispute the court-appointed psychiatrist's finding that he is mentally competent to understand the nature and consequences of the charge against him.

His next court hearing is scheduled for early December, but any trial is expected to take place in California, where the federal charge was filed.

Inside the storage units in Los Angeles the FBI says agents found about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.

In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades.

Markle has called the allegations "sick lies".

He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated.

On Monday, police in the Philippines asked prosecutors to charge Markle with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.

Last month, police there obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018, and he did not attend her wedding in London that same year.

The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

articles.title: Trigony House House hotel seeks new life as bookings hit 'negligible level'
articles.summary: Trigony House Hotel - a building dating back to the 18th Century - could become a private home.
articles.body:
A historic country house hotel in the south of Scotland is seeking a new use after its future bookings reached a "negligible level".

Plans have been lodged to convert the Trigony House Hotel near Thornhill - which dates back to at least the 18th Century - into a private home.

A statement submitted with the proposals said the decision had been made after a period of "very significant trading losses" with future bookings on an "even more downward trend".

It added that the use of the hotel had been at such levels that its conversion would not mean there was "any loss of community facility".

The hotel's story goes back hundreds of years to the 1700s when it was the shooting and fishing lodge for Closeburn Castle.

The plans would not see any changes to the structure of any buildings or the gardens and grounds.
